appearance_facts.fact: Chart title is 'Units Sold by Product (Weekend Pop-up)' in bold, black text at the top of the chart.
Y-axis label is 'Units Sold' in black text, vertically aligned along the left side of the chart.
X-axis label is 'Product' in black text, horizontally aligned below the bar chart.
Y-axis has major ticks at 2,000, 4,000, 6,000, 8,000, and 10,000, with gridlines at each major tick.
X-axis has labels for five products: 'Product A', 'Product B', 'Product C', 'Product D', and 'Product E', positioned below each respective bar.
All bars are solid dark red.
Bar for 'Product A' reaches approximately 1,800 units on the y-axis, below the 2,000 mark.
Bar for 'Product C' reaches approximately 2,200 units on the y-axis, slightly above the 2,000 mark.

printed_facts.fact: The y-axis scale is linear, with units marked in increments of 2,000 from 0 to 10,000.
Bar for 'Product B' reaches exactly 6,000 units on the y-axis.
Bar for 'Product D' reaches exactly 10,000 units on the y-axis.
Bar for 'Product E' reaches exactly 8,000 units on the y-axis.

Policy table defines thresholds: <1,000 units = Critical sales escalation; >=1,000 and <2,000 = Low-sales review; <500 from threshold = Manual check; >=6,000 and <9,000 = Expanded replenishment; >=9,000 = Growth allocation.

public_definitions: goal: Review the weekend pop-up Units Sold by Product dashboard, then complete the Product A merchandising review intake by selecting the appropriate product route.
chart_reference: Use the Units Sold by Product dashboard as the evidence source for the Product A merchandising route.

option_labels: Open Product A low-sales review, Route Product A to critical sales escalation, Keep Product A on regular merchandising plan, Route Product A to expanded replenishment planning, Route Product A to growth allocation review, Flag Product A for manual merchandising check
policy_tables: Merchandising policy levels with unit condition thresholds and corresponding routes.
